description: We are building FIRETRACE for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (CH-09): a reliable historical fire-activity calendar using harmonised MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. Our work combines geospatial data, statistical analysis, visualisation and an interactive web application. We welcome collaborators interested in Earth science, GIS, data analysis, statistics, software development, UI/UX and science communication. Join us to turn satellite data into clear, evidence-based insights.
summary:
PYROTRACE harmonizes active-fire observations from four NASA satellite 
sensors — MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua, VIIRS NOAA-20 and VIIRS NOAA-21 — 
into one consistent, comparable fire-activity record for Kerala, India.

The core problem: VIIRS pixels are 375 m versus MODIS at 1 km. VIIRS 
detects smaller fires, making raw detection counts 3–5× higher for the 
same burning activity. Every historical fire trend built from raw counts 
carries this artifact silently. NASA's Suomi NPP satellite stopped 
transmitting on November 1, 2026 — fourteen days before this hackathon — 
creating a third sensor transition in the 24-year record.

PYROTRACE addresses this by aggregating MODIS and VIIRS detections onto 
a common 0.05° spatial grid, counting unique active cell-days per sensor, 
and applying regional calibration using the sensor overlap period. A 
Sensor Truth Lab displays raw versus harmonized records side by side, 
making the correction visible rather than hidden.

The platform uses real NASA FIRMS data: 25 Kerala fire detections across 
all four sensors from November 2026, correctly showing Kerala's low 
pre-season baseline with transparent uncertainty at every step.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

PYROTRACE is a satellite fire-intelligence platform that solves a concrete scientific problem: NASA MODIS and VIIRS sensors observe fires differently, making their raw detection counts incomparable across time.

VIIRS pixels are 375 m versus MODIS at 1 km — VIIRS detects smaller fires, inflating counts 3–5× for identical burning activity. Every raw historical fire trend carries this artifact. With Suomi NPP ending science data delivery on November 1, 2026 and MODIS missions nearing their end, cross-sensor continuity is an urgent operational problem happening right now.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data ingestion — MODIS C6.1, VIIRS NOAA-20 C2 and VIIRS NOAA-21 C2 active-fire observations downloaded from NASA FIRMS for Kerala, India

2. Grid aggregation — detections mapped to a common 0.05° spatial grid; unique active cell-days counted per sensor per day, eliminating pixel-size inflation

3. Sensor calibration — regional calibration factor calculated from the MODIS–VIIRS overlap period using median ratio and MAD uncertainty

4. Sensor Truth Lab — raw versus harmonized records displayed side by side so the correction is visible, not hidden inside a finished chart

5. Historical calendar — seasonal fire patterns visualized with anomaly detection using robust median and MAD statistical methods

6. Methodology page — every formula documented with known limitations stated transparently

REAL DATA

25 Kerala fire detections from November 7–13, 2026 across all four sensors: MODIS Terra, MODIS Aqua, VIIRS NOAA-20 and VIIRS NOAA-21. November is correctly shown as Kerala's low pre-season baseline. The February–April peak fire season is documented in the historical calendar view. Source: NASA FIRMS active fire data.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

PYROTRACE makes the sensor transition problem visible and correctable for researchers, forest officers and disaster-response teams who rely on historical fire records. By showing raw versus harmonized records side by side with transparent uncertainty, it builds trust in the corrected output. The methodology is documented and reproducible. The platform architecture supports extension to any global region using the same NASA FIRMS data pipeline.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • Charts: Recharts
  • Maps: Leaflet, React-Leaflet, OpenStreetMap
  • Data processing: Python, Pandas
  • Data source: NASA FIRMS API — MODIS C6.1, VIIRS NOAA-20 C2, VIIRS
  • NOAA-21 C2 (CSV format, South Asia region)
  • Deployment: Vercel
  • Source control: GitHub

CREATIVE APPROACH

Instead of building another fire hotspot map, PYROTRACE makes the measurement problem the central experience. The Sensor Truth Lab lets any user — researcher, judge or student — see exactly where the artificial sensor gap comes from, what the correction does, and how reliable that correction is. The science is not hidden. Scientific honesty is treated as a feature, not a disclaimer. Every statistic on the platform is calculated from loaded NASA data — no fabricated numbers appear anywhere in the application.

SCIENTIFIC PRINCIPLES FOLLOWED

  • Active cell-days formula: A(s,t) = Σ I(cell g has ≥1 detection from sensor s on date t), summed over all grid cells in the AOI
  • Calibration: R = median(A_MODIS / A_VIIRS) during overlap period
  • Anomaly score: z = (observed − median_historical) / MAD_historical
  • Active cell-days are satellite observations, not confirmed wildfires
  • Cloud cover, overpass time, confidence flags and grid resolution all affect results and are documented as limitations

Source code: https://github.com/sanjay-sanju-03/PYROTRACE.git

Live application: https://pyrotrace.vercel.app/
